confirmed.title: The collapse kill is a per-FRAME sum tested against a fixed constant, so a slow frame destroys the pot
confirmed.repro: Turn the assist off. Throw a 2400 g pot: open it, then run about twenty lift passes with wet hands. Wind the wheel to the top of the dial (190 rpm). The piece reads 20.8 cm tall with a 3.7 mm minimum wall and sits there indefinitely at 30 fps or better. The instant one frame takes 50 ms — which is where main.js's own adaptive-quality code drops the pixel ratio (fps < 26), and where Safari on an iPad lands under load — the very next frame prints 'The wall let go. The whole thing came down in a spiral.' and the pot is gone. The player changed nothing; the frame just took longer. Conversely a 120 Hz iPad Pro tolerates exactly twice the over-stress a 60 Hz desktop does, so the same pot is a different game on two devices.
confirmed.arithmetic: `let collapse = 0;` is declared at line 1044, INSIDE step(), so it is reset every frame. Lines 1076-1118 add `min(3.5, stress_i - 1) * dt` for every over-stressed section, then line 1158 compares that one-frame sum to a constant. The test is therefore `SUM_i over_i > threshold / dt` — the pot's tolerance is inversely proportional to frame length. Non-assist threshold 0.9: at 120fps it needs SUM(over) > 108; at 60fps > 54; at 30fps > 27; at 20fps (dt = 0.05, exactly the clamp at src/main.js:170 `const dt = Math.min(0.05, (now - last) / 1000)`) it needs only > 18. That is a 6x swing in difficulty from frame rate alone. Measured on a pot thrown through the real Hand class, assist off, 2400 g, 20 lift passes with the water tool, wheel at MAX_RPM 190 = 19.90 rad/s (game.js:29 caps it there): SUM(over) = 20.0 -> 20.0*(1/120)=0.17 ok, 20.0*(1/60)=0.33 ok, 20.0*(1/45)=0.44 ok, 20.0*(1/30)=0.67 ok, 20.0*0.05=1.00 > 0.9 DEAD. Confirmed by running it: 120fps ok, 60fps ok, 45fps ok, 30fps ok, 20fps DEAD.

- src/sim/clay.js:1077 `        const over = Math.min(3.5, s - 1);` — matches the claimed `min(3.5, stress_i - 1)`.
- src/sim/clay.js:1118 `        collapse += over * dt;` — exact, including the `* dt`.
- src/sim/clay.js:1158-1159 `      if (collapse > (forgiving ? 1.7 : 0.9)) {` / `        this.kill('The wall let go. The whole thing came down in a spiral.');` — exact, thresholds 1.7/0.9 as claimed.

Supporting citations also verified:
- src/main.js:170 `    const dt = Math.min(0.05, (now - last) / 1000);` — exact, so worst-case dt really is 0.05.
- src/game/game.js:29 `const MAX_RPM = 190;` — exact; 190 rpm = 19.897 rad/s, matching the claimed 19.90.
- src/game/game.js:1466 `    c.step(dt, this.omega, { dryRate: assist ? 0.34 : 1, forgiving: assist });` — I checked specifically for sub-stepping, since a fixed-dt inner loop would have killed the frame-rate dependence even with the quote correct. The structural defect is therefore real as stated: since dt factors out of the sum, the test reduces to SUM_i(over_i) > threshold/dt, i.e. 0.9/dt — SUM > 108 at 120fps, > 54 at 60fps, > 27 at 30fps, > 18 at dt=0.05. The `* dt` only makes sense for a value that persists across frames, and this one does not; the neighbouring accumulators in the same loop (this.scar[i], this.stats.tears += dt) are persistent, which makes the local `collapse` the odd one out.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT on the repro's specific numbers, which I could not reproduce and which the fixer should not trust: I drove the real Clay through the harness geometry (centre, open, floor-widen, lift passes) at masses 1200/1800/2400 and measured SUM(over) at 190 rpm by replicating the stress loop exactly. Best real thrown pot I reached was SUM(over) = 7.03 (18 sections over, max stress 1.87) on a 45.5 cm / 3.52 mm-wall piece; the 1200/1800/2400 g pots gave 0.00 / 0.87 / 2.35. Running those states at 190 rpm with assist off for 10 s survived at all of 120/60/30/20 fps. So I could not reach the claimed SUM(over) = 20.0, and the "20 fps DEAD" line in the candidate did not reproduce for me — pots that stressed tended to trip the MAX_H = 46 kill ("It grew past what wet clay can hold and folded on itself") first. The dt-scaled threshold is definitely in the code; whether a player can actually park a pot in the 18-54 band is not something I could demonstrate. Report the mechanism and the line numbers, not the "SUM(over) = 20.0, confirmed by running it" figure.

CONFIRMED — I tried to break it and could not. The mechanism, the arithmetic and the player-visible consequence all hold. Only the candidate's specific pot recipe is wrong, and I have a working replacement.

WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE BYTES
The quoted code is real and unmodified:
  src/sim/clay.js:1044   `    let collapse = 0;`            (inside step(), so reset every frame)
  src/sim/clay.js:1118   `        collapse += over * dt;`
  src/sim/clay.js:1158   `      if (collapse > (forgiving ? 1.7 : 0.9)) {`
`collapse` appears at exactly those three lines and nowhere else (grep -n "collapse" over src/) — a local declared and consumed inside one call, never a member. So the test is literally `dt * SUM_i(min(3.5, stress_i - 1)) > threshold`, i.e. `SUM(over) > threshold / dt`.

THE dt PATH IS UNSUBDIVIDED AND REACHES 0.05
  src/main.js:170  `    const dt = Math.min(0.05, (now - last) / 1000);`
  src/game/game.js:1236 `update(dt)` -> `_updateThrow(dt)` -> src/game/game.js:1466 `c.step(dt, this.omega, { dryRate: assist ? 0.34 : 1, forgiving: assist });`
No accumulator, no fixed timestep, no substepping anywhere on that path. `.step(` in src/ appears only at game.js:1466 and in the dev benches. There is no visibilitychange pause either, so a refocused tab also lands on dt=0.05.

ARITHMETIC, REDONE FROM SCRATCH
Assist off (0.9):  >108 @120fps, >54 @60, >40.5 @45, >27 @30, >18 @20 (dt clamped 0.05).
Assist ON  (1.7):  >204 @120fps, >102 @60, >76.5 @45, >51 @30, >34 @20.
The candidate's four numbers (108/54/27/18) are all correct. MAX_RPM 190 (game.js:29, clamped game.js:517) = 19.897 rad/s, also correct.

REPRODUCED WITH THE REAL HAND, ASSIST OFF
Driving harness.mjs (which drives the same `Hand` the game does) with forgiving:false, dryRate:1, then the water tool, then the wheel at 190 rpm — a 10 s hold, no player input:
  600 g, H=20.6cm D=17.2cm meanWall=4.2mm wet=0.81 -> SUM(over)=31.8
      120fps ok | 60fps ok | 45fps ok | 30fps DEAD (frame 1) | 20fps DEAD (frame 1)
  750 g, H=22.3 D=18.0 meanWall=5.5mm wet=0.80 -> SUM=22.3
      120 ok | 60 ok | 45 ok | 30 ok | 20fps DEAD
  500 g -> SUM=54.4: 120 ok, everything 60 and below DEAD.
  400 g -> SUM=105.8: only 120fps survives.
Message every time: "The wall let go. The whole thing came down in a spiral."

IT IS NOT CONFINED TO ASSIST-OFF. On the DEFAULT path (game.js:1174 `assist !== false`, so forgiving:true/dryRate 0.34):
  400 g, H=21.2 D=15.3 meanWall=2.4mm wet=0.82 -> SUM=75.2: 120 ok, 60 ok, 45 ok, 30fps DEAD, 20fps DEAD.
  350 g -> SUM=103.9: 120fps ok, 60fps DEAD.

THE PLAYER WOULD ABSOLUTELY SEE IT — AND SEE THE RECOVERY THEY WERE DENIED
The dynamics are strongly self-healing, which is what makes this cruel rather than merely inconsistent. From SUM(over)=35.6 at 190 rpm, at 60fps SUM decays monotonically to 0 in 6.8 s: the wall thickens 2.00mm -> 2.50mm, height eases 20.8 -> 17.6 cm, maxStress falls 1.57 -> 0.88, and the pot lives, permanently. The same pot at 30fps is destroyed on the first frame.
Injecting exactly ONE 50 ms frame into an otherwise clean 60fps run of that recovery:
  spike at frame 1 (t=0.02s) DEAD | frame 5 DEAD | frame 15 DEAD | frame 30 DEAD | frame 60 (t=1.00s) DEAD | frame 120 (t=2.00s) survives.
So there is a ~1.3-second window on every stressed pot in which a single dropped frame is fatal. 50 ms is not exotic on the target device: main.js's own adaptive-quality block sheds SMAA at fps<34 (29 ms) and halves the pixel ratio at fps<26 (38 ms), so the author already budgets for sub-30fps, and the pixel-ratio change itself costs a frame.

INTERNAL EVIDENCE THIS IS A MISTAKE, NOT A DESIGN CHOICE
Every other kill in the same block at clay.js:1155-1176 tests STATE and is frame-rate independent: `this.height > MAX_H`, `this.maxR > 26`, `met.wobble > 1.9`, and the `torn` count of sections with scar>0.985. `collapse` is the only one multiplied by dt. And the file demonstrates elsewhere that the author knows how to write a real accumulator — `this.stats.tears += dt` (line 1130) and `this.stats.wobbleIntegral += o * dt * 0.02` (line 1147) are persistent members. `collapse` was written with accumulator syntax (`+=`, `* dt`) but function-local scope, so it has no dt->0 limit at all: as the frame gets shorter the kill becomes unreachable, and as it lengthens toward the 0.05 clamp it becomes 3x easier than at 60fps.

CORRECTIONS THE REPORT NEEDS
The candidate's recipe does not reproduce. I threw a 2400 g pot through the real Hand with assist off (H=27.2cm, D=19.1cm, minWall=3.74mm, wet=0.76) and got SUM(over)=3.97 at 190 rpm — it survives at every frame rate including the 0.05 clamp. A 2400 g pot cannot be thin, wide and under MAX_H=46 at the same time: at D=19 a 4 mm wall consumes only 23.9 cm3 per cm of height, so 1250 cm3 of clay would stand 52 cm tall. The band is reached by SMALL pots, 350-750 g, not 2400 g. The candidate's "SUM(over) = 20.0 ... 30fps ok, 20fps DEAD" is arithmetically self-consistent (20*0.0333=0.67 < 0.9; 20*0.05=1.00 > 0.9) but is not the pot described, so the repro steps should be replaced with the 600 g / 190 rpm case above. Its other claim — that a 120 Hz iPad Pro tolerates exactly twice the over-stress a 60 Hz desktop does — is correct, and I confirmed the reverse too (350 g assist-on pot: survives at 120fps, destroyed at 60fps).

confirmed.title: Viewing a shelf piece from the pause menu overwrites the glaze you are working on
confirmed.repro: Get one pot onto the shelf, then start a new commission and reach the glaze room. Dip and brush until the pot is 70% covered and the foot is wiped. Press Esc -> The shelf -> tap the piece on the shelf (this calls showPiece, game.js:2648 `dressPot(this, p);`). Tap Back to the shelf -> Back -> Back to work. The state is still ST.GLAZE, but GlazeField.restore() (glazeField.js:454-472) has written over EVERY cell of this.field.data with the shelf piece's saved 64x48 field, stretched onto the current pot. Your glazing is gone and replaced by the old piece's. field.clear() is only called in startGlaze() (game.js:1750), which is not re-entered — and the code itself notes at game.js:1811 that 'the glaze room has no undo'. openMenu() does not even offer 'Wedge it again' outside THROW/TRIM (game.js:1106), so the only way out is to abandon the commission. The firing then uses the foreign field: openKiln reads this.field.stats() for the appraisal and _updateFiring flows it.
confirmed.arithmetic: restore() loops j=0..GH-1, i=0..GW-1 and assigns this.data[o+c] unconditionally — 100% of the field is overwritten, not merged. dressPot is called from showPiece with no state guard; showGallery is bound in openMenu (game.js:1117) for every state including ST.GLAZE.
whyItStood:
The quoted code exists byte-for-byte at the cited path and line. `cat -A` on src/game/piece.js lines 20-30 confirms, with `grep -n` giving the exact anchors: line 22 `export function dressPot(game, p) {`, 23 `  const c = Clay.fromSnapshot(p.clay);`, 24 `  game.pb.build(c);`, 25 blank, 26 `  game.field.restore(p.field);`, 27 `  game.field.upload?.();`. The accused line 26 is exactly where the candidate says it is. md5 of the file is 57d7291fe7f555817abc99f8e8892233; last commit touching it is e8277de "Look at what you made, and put your name on it" — the file has not moved on.

Every supporting citation also checks out against the real bytes:
- game.js:2648 is `    dressPot(this, p);`, inside `showPiece(p, back)`. The only guard above it is `if (!p || !p.clay) { back(); return; }` — a guard on the SHELF piece, not on `this.state`. No state check exists.
- glazeField.js:454-472 is `restore(snap)` exactly as described. It loops `for (let j = 0; j < GH; j++)` / `for (let i = 0; i < GW; i++)` and assigns `this.data[o + c] = (bin.charCodeAt(q + c) / 255) * 0.7;` unconditionally — no merge, no mask, no early-out. GW=192, GH=160 (glazeField.js:20-21), so all 192x160 = 30,720 cells / 122,880 bytes are overwritten from the 64x48 source snapshot, nearest-neighbour stretched. 100% overwrite, as claimed.
- game.js:1750 `this.field.clear();` sits in startGlaze, followed by `this.state = ST.GLAZE` — confirmed not re-entered by the view path.
- game.js:1106 is the `? '<button data-a="rethrow">...` line, gated by `${this.state === ST.THROW || this.state === ST.TRIM` on 1105 — "Wedge it again" genuinely is not offered in ST.GLAZE.
- game.js:1117 is `if (a === 'gallery') this.showGallery(() => this.openMenu());` with no state condition — reachable from ST.GLAZE.

I looked specifically for anything that would neutralize this and found nothing. `field.snapshot()` is called in exactly one place, game.js:2520, in the kiln-exit save path — the working field is never snapshotted before showPiece, so there is nothing to roll back from. The exit path (game.js:2677-2681) only does `this._viewing = null;`, removes the `viewing` class, and calls `back()`; it does not restore the field or rebuild the working pot.

The damage is in fact broader than the candidate argued. piece.js:24 `game.pb.build(c)` also rebuilds the pot geometry from the shelf piece's clay, and `this.field.bindProfile(this.pb)` is only called at game.js:769, 1751 and 2396 — never on the return path — so the field stays bound to a profile that no longer matches. dressPot also forces `u.uFired.value = 1; u.uWet.value = 0; u.uBisque.value = 1; u.uVitrified.value = 1;` and overwrites uBodyCol/uBodyCol2 with the shelf piece's body, none of which are reset on the way back, so the in-progress pot returns looking fired and in the wrong clay colour.

One citation in the repro prose is off: the "the glaze room has no undo" comment is at game.js:1825, not 1811. That is a 14-line drift in a supporting quote of a comment, not in the accused code, and it does not affect the finding.

Verdict: not refuted. The code is present exactly as quoted and the mechanism is real.

CONFIRMED — I could not break it. I attacked eight escape hatches and every one closed.

1) Is the code as quoted? Yes, byte-exact. `src/game/piece.js:22-27`:
   22: `export function dressPot(game, p) {`
   23: `  const c = Clay.fromSnapshot(p.clay);`
   24: `  game.pb.build(c);`
   26: `  game.field.restore(p.field);`
   27: `  game.field.upload?.();`
   And `src/game/game.js:2648: dressPot(this, p);` inside `showPiece(p, back)` (2638). The only guard in showPiece is `if (!p || !p.clay) { back(); return; }` (2639) — no state check.

2) Does restore() really clobber 100%? Yes. `src/sim/glazeField.js:454-472` loops `j=0..GH-1`, `i=0..GW-1` and does `this.data[o+c] = (bin.charCodeAt(q+c)/255)*0.7` unconditionally — no merge, no alpha test, no early-out. GW=192, GH=160 (glazeField.js:20-21), so all 192*160*4 = 122,880 floats are rewritten from the shelf piece's 64x48 snapshot by nearest-neighbour stretch.

3) Best refutation attempt — maybe `p.field` is absent so restore() bails at line 456 `if (!snap || !snap.d) return false;`. It is NOT absent: `src/game/game.js:2520` writes `field: this.field.snapshot(),` into every `s.gallery.push({...})` (2508-2527), and save.js never strips it (save.js:96-111 only slices the array on quota). So `snap.d` is a real base64 string and restore runs to completion.

4) Is the path reachable in ST.GLAZE? Yes, on desktop. `window.addEventListener('keydown', ...)` is attached unconditionally at game.js:469; `_onKey` line 490 is `if (k === 'Escape') { this.openMenu(); return; }` with no state gate (the only early return above it is `if (this.hud.overlayOpen)`, which is false while glazing). `openMenu()` line 1117 is `if (a === 'gallery') this.showGallery(() => this.openMenu());` — bound for every state. showGallery:2625 calls `this.showPiece(...)`. Caveat worth passing on: on iPad there is no on-screen menu affordance during ST.GLAZE (index.html has only `#bare-toggle` and `#advance`; every `data-a="menu"` at 1069/1698/2581 lives inside an overlay), so this is a desktop/hardware-keyboard repro, not a bare-iPad one.

5) Does anything put it back? No. `field.clear()` exists at exactly three sites — game.js:768, 1144 (startThrow), 1750 (startGlaze). None is re-entered. `resume` is `if (a === 'resume') this.hud.closeOverlay();` (1116), and `closeOverlay()` (hud.js:876-879) only strips a class and empties `ovInner`. `showPiece`'s Back handler (2678-2681) clears `_viewing` and the `viewing` class and nothing else. `_updateGlaze` (1978+) never rebuilds or re-clears the field.

6) Would the player see it? Yes, on the next frame. `game.js:109` binds `this.mat.userData.u.uGlaze.value = this.field.tex` and potMaterial.js:212 samples `texture2D(uGlaze, guv)`. restore() calls `this._push()` (line 469); `_push` (407-427) uses `lo = this.dirty ? this._lo : 0` — and `dirty` is false at that moment because the glaze loop uploads every frame — so it converts rows 0..GH-1 and sets `tex.needsUpdate = true`. Full repaint, immediately.

7) Does it poison the outcome, not just the picture? Yes. `openKiln()` (2415) line 2431 `const gs = this.field.stats();` feeds `appraise({... glazeStats: gs ...})` (2443+), and `_startFiring` line 2266 sets `this._preStats = this.field.stats();`. Also `this.field.footRisk()` (2435) can now flip `destroyed = true` off a foreign field.

8) Is there a way out? No. game.js:1105-1107 gates the rethrow button on `this.state === ST.THROW || this.state === ST.TRIM`, so in ST.GLAZE the menu offers resume / shelf / codex / how / title only. Abandoning the commission is the only exit. The code's own note at game.js:1825 reads "the glaze room has no undo" (the candidate said 1811 — a 14-line slip in the prose, the substance is correct).

EXTRA, corroborating and worth adding to the report: `dressPot` calls `game.pb.build(c)`, not `pb.update(c)`. In `src/render/potMesh.js`, `build()` (120-169) only fills the CPU meridian arrays and never touches the texture; only `update()` (172-231) ends with `this.tex.needsUpdate = true` (line 230). Two consequences. (a) While viewing a shelf piece you are looking at your CURRENT pot's silhouette wearing the shelf piece's glaze — the shape never changes. (b) After you return to the glaze room, `pb.pr`/`pb.py` describe the SHELF piece, and `raycastPot(org, dir, this.pb)` in `_updateGlaze` (line ~2010) marches against those arrays — so the brush cursor and every stroke now land against a meridian that is not the pot on screen. The glaze field is also still bound to the old profile (`bindProfile` ran once in startGlaze:1751).

THROW/TRIM are not affected in the same way: `_updateThrow` re-runs `pb.update(this.clay)` so the meridian self-heals, the field is unused before glazing, and `startGlaze` calls `field.clear()` at 1750. ST.GLAZE and ST.KILN are the vulnerable states, and ST.KILN is worse because the damage is invisible until the appraisal.

Severity as filed (breaks-the-game) is right. Confidence: high — traced end to end, every line re-read off the bytes with sed/grep.

confirmed.title: Escape on the 'Break everything' confirmation erases the save
confirmed.repro: On the title screen click 'Break everything and start again'. The confirmation appears with two buttons (game.js:824-825): `<button class="btn" data-a="no">No</button>` and `<button class="btn primary" data-a="yes">Break it</button>`. Press Escape — the universal cancel key, and the key this game itself binds to 'menu'/'back' everywhere else. _onKey sees overlayOpen, finds `.btn.primary` (which is 'Break it'), and clicks it: SaveIO.wipe() runs, the shelf, codex, standing and ash-marks are gone, unrecoverably. Escape is bound to the destructive choice on the one screen in the game that asks 'Are you sure'. The same rule fires the irreversible primary on every other overlay too: Escape on the results card clicks 'Next commission', advancing the day and closing the report you were reading.

confirmed.title: The anti-ruin fuel guard measures the previous pot's glazes and wall, not this one's
confirmed.repro: _floorFiring is called only from _fuelAdvance (game.js:970), which is called only from nextCommission (1014) and _buyClay (956). this.slots and this.clay are reset in startThrow (game.js:1144-1147), which runs AFTER both — so at both call sites they still hold the pot you just finished. On the first commission of a session they hold the title-screen decoration: _demoPot sets `this.slots = [GLAZE_BY_ID.celadon, null, null]` and a 21.5 cm demo jar. Repro: finish a pot glazed in Raku Copper Matte on a thin wall, arrive at the next commission broke. The guard prices raku's 952 C firing, advances you to 51 marks, and you then throw a heavy-walled pot and glaze it in Ninth Ash. lightKiln (game.js:2244) refuses: 'That firing costs 53 ash-marks and you have 51.' In guild mode the schedule sliders are not on screen, so there is nothing to turn down and no second advance — exactly the dead run the docstring above this function says it exists to prevent ('Below this the run is over... nothing in the interface tells them the game has ended'). The `GLAZE_BY_ID[wanted]` fallback that WOULD have used the brief's required glaze is unreachable: no path reaches _floorFiring with this.slots all null.

notReached.repro: Throwing room, default settings (save.js:57 has assist:true), default tool (hands). Drag the WHEEL bar — the pedal wired up at hud.js:106-121 — all the way to the right. The gauge shoots up and then slides back down on its own over about two seconds, with nothing touching it. Same with the scroll wheel, and same with W and S — and the game's own toast on the very next line promises otherwise: game.js:1384 'The wheel finds its own speed, slowing as the pot opens out. W and S to take it over.' Nothing anywhere turns the assist off when the player takes it over. On an iPad this is worse than a nuisance: the touch hint map (hud.js:252-262) drops SHIFT+SCROLL, TAB, SPACE and CTRL+Z and rewrites SCROLL as 'PINCH zoom', so the pedal is the only wheel control a tablet player has, and it is the inert one.

notReached.title: The drag pedal is a 7px-tall touch target — the one gauge the coarse-pointer stylesheet does not enlarge
notReached.repro: iPad, throwing room. Try to drag the WHEEL bar to change the speed. It is 7 CSS px tall — the only interactive gauge in the game, and the ONLY one made SHORTER than the read-only ones (.gauge .bar is height:12px at style.css:279). `grep -n pedal src/ui/style.css` returns exactly three hits, 287/291/292, none of them inside a @media (pointer:coarse) block; the coarse block at style.css:804-819 goes out of its way to bump .tool to 60x66, .btn padding to 1.15em/1.7em, and input[type=range] to height:34px with 26px thumbs. The pedal was missed. Its only other affordance, .gauge.pedal .bar:hover at style.css:291, is a hover state, which a finger does not have — so on a tablet there is nothing to see and almost nothing to hit.

notReached.title: step() runs three full-strength box blurs per frame with no dt, so the pot heals itself twice as fast on a 120 Hz screen
notReached.repro: Knock the rim off true so there is one visible lump, take the hand off the clay entirely and let the wheel turn for ten seconds. On a 120 Hz iPad the lump is 0.010 cm; on a 60 Hz display it is 0.014 cm; at 30 fps it is 0.020 cm. The pot repairs itself at whatever rate the screen refreshes, with no input at all — and the clay softens and equalises at that same rate, so plasticity under the hand differs by device.

notReached.title: open() is the one smoothing call that forgets the `amount` argument, so it blurs the bore outright every frame
notReached.repro: Press down into the middle of a fresh lump and hold. The shoulder where the floor turns into the wall softens upward at a rate set by the refresh rate rather than by how long or how hard you pressed. The same opening stroke leaves a measurably different floor on a 120 Hz iPad than on a 60 Hz desktop.

notReached.title: _smoothProfile never smooths the inner wall — the branch that would is unreachable
notReached.repro: Cut a step into the wall with a jerky stroke, then hold the rib on it. The outer silhouette comes clean; the bore keeps the step. Grep confirms it: `grep -n '_smoothProfile' src/sim/clay.js` gives 376, 707, 787, 912 — every caller passes 0.

notReached.title: One codex fragment can never be unlocked — stats.drowned is never incremented anywhere
notReached.repro: `grep -rn drowned src/` returns exactly two hits in the whole codebase: this predicate, and `drowned: 0` in the blankSave initializer (save.js:58). Nothing ever writes it — not clay.js (which tracks stats.waterUsed but never reports it up), not _updateThrow, not _collapse. The other six CODEX predicates all read counters that are written (stats.centred at game.js:1598, stats.collapses at 1683, firings at 1753, crazed at 2469/2482, best at 2468). So 'On too much water' is dead: a player who reads the title screen sees 'The codex — N FRAGMENTS' and can drive N to at most 6 of the 7 play-unlocked fragments however long they play, with nothing to tell them which one is missing or why.

notReached.title: The water sound flag is cleared before the audio mixer ever reads it
notReached.repro: quickWater is set only in _onKey (game.js:509, `if (this.state === ST.THROW) { this.quickWater = true; }` — the SPACE key advertised as 'SPACE water' in the key hints). Inside one update(dt), the state switch runs _updateThrow FIRST, which reads it at game.js:1364 (`const tId = this.quickWater ? 'water' : this.toolId;`) and then clears it at game.js:1451 (`this.quickWater = false;`). Only afterwards, at game.js:1314, does audio.update read it — by which time it is unconditionally false. Keydown handlers run between rAF callbacks, so there is no interleaving that saves it. The `this.quickWater ||` half of that condition can never evaluate true: holding SPACE applies water to the clay but never opens the water loop (audio.js:320 `this.s.water.g.gain.setTargetAtTime(clamp01(s.water ?? 0) * 0.30, ...)`), so the one control that has no on-screen tool icon is also the one with no sound.

notReached.title: The TOUCH block is no longer last: .glaze's coarse-pointer padding is dead on both iPad orientations
notReached.repro: This is the third occurrence of the fault whose fix the file documents twice ('THIS BLOCK MUST STAY AT THE END OF THE FILE'). Two blocks have since been appended after @media (pointer:coarse): line 1161 '@media (max-height: 900px), (max-width: 900px){ .glaze{padding:.2em .4em} }' and line 1172 '@media (max-height: 680px){ .glaze{...padding:.16em .3em} }'. Equal specificity, later wins — and an iPad matches the 900px block in BOTH orientations (834 wide in portrait, 834 tall in landscape). So the one enlargement made for fingers on the control the whole glazing phase runs through never applies on the device it was written for.

notReached.title: The Hide-panels button — the control added for the iPad complaint — is a 31px touch target
notReached.repro: On the iPad, the button that folds the panels away sits in the bottom-right corner. Its own stylesheet declares 44px as the floor for a thumb ('44px is the size everyone converged on', line 803), and the coarse-pointer bump here takes it to 31px. Its contents are an 11px icon box and an 11px/1 line of type, so the padding is all there is.

notReached.title: S.irid is computed every frame and never read; mat.iridescence is never set, so the iridescence path the comment claims to force is never compiled
notReached.repro: Fire an oil-spot, hematite or any metallic glaze (uSlotQ.z / uSlotR.x / uSlotS.z > 0). The shader raises S.irid for exactly those pixels and nothing consumes it — the glaze reads as flat metal-tinted colour with no thin-film shift. Verified by running onBeforeCompile: 'celIrid' occurs exactly once in the patched fragment shader, which is its own declaration at potMaterial.js:619 ('float celIrid = S.irid;'). There is no .replace() anywhere in the file that writes material.iridescence.

notReached.title: Studio._mat() silently drops every normalMap and roughnessMap handed to it, so all six tuned normalScale values in the room are dead
notReached.repro: Look at the sponge on the bench. studio.js:558-562 builds it with clothMaps and normalScale (2.2, 2.2) under a comment saying 'The cloth maps give it a tooth' — it has no tooth, it is a flat-shaded lumpy blob. Same for the floor (normalScale 0.8, line 134), the plaster walls (1.1, line 147), the wheel head (0.45, line 302), the bucket (0.7, line 582) and the kiln bricks (1.15, line 776). _mat reads only maps.map from its first argument; normalMap and roughnessMap are passed in that same first argument at every call site and never copied onto the material. normalScale arrives via ...o and three ignores it because USE_NORMALMAP is never defined.

notReached.title: The flywheel turns at 0.42x the wheel head despite a rigid shaft drawn between them
notReached.repro: Kick the wheel up to speed and crouch (drag down until the splash pan fades) so both the head and the flywheel are in frame. The three spokes on the flywheel visibly lag the head's texture. studio.js:434-439 builds a solid CylinderGeometry(2.6, 3.6, 40) shaft joining the two, and studio.js:428 a stretcher ring — there is no gearing anywhere in the model, so a kick wheel's flywheel and head are on one shaft at 1:1. No comment in the file defends the 0.42, and every other deliberate deviation here is commented at length.

notReached.title: The two-finger banding-wheel flick uses a magic *22 where the mouse path divides by real elapsed time
notReached.repro: Glaze room. Flick the pot with a right-button mouse drag at a moderate speed and let go — it coasts about 83 degrees. Do the same flick with two fingers on the iPad and it coasts 40 degrees on a 60Hz iPad, 20 degrees on a 120Hz iPad Pro. Same gesture, same speed, three different amounts of coast, and the tablet is always the weakest. Directly above it, game.js:259-262 solves exactly this for the mouse and the comment at game.js:242-249 explains why per-event deltas without elapsed time are wrong; the touch branch reintroduces it.

notReached.title: A mouse pointercancel leaves pointer.right stuck true — the camera then orbits with no button held
notReached.repro: Desktop. Hold the right button and drag to orbit. If a pointercancel is dispatched for that pointer instead of a pointerup — the browser starting a native drag, the OS taking the pointer — the branch that clears pointer.right never runs, because the Pointer Events spec sets button to -1 on pointercancel (buttons 0), not to 2. Control falls to game.js:442-443, which clears pointer.down (already false) and fires a phantom _onRelease(). From that moment every bare mouse move orbits the studio with nothing pressed, and the only way out is to blur the window (game.js:447-450). Both listeners share one handler — game.js:445-446 `c.addEventListener('pointerup', up); c.addEventListener('pointercancel', up);` — so the handler cannot tell the two apart, and there is no lostpointercapture listener anywhere in the file to catch it either. The touch path is symmetrical and safe here; only the mouse/pen path reads e.button.

notReached.title: clay.stats is labelled 'used by scoring' but scoring.js never mentions stats at all
notReached.repro: Nothing the player sees, but the comment claims a consumer that does not exist, and per-frame work is being spent maintaining it. If a scoring rule was ever meant to reward 'you pulled it up cleanly' or 'you watered it too much', it silently does not.

notReached.title: ProfileBuffer.radiiAt is dead, and would return a rim radius for y = 0 if it were called
notReached.repro: Not reachable today because nothing calls it. Flagged because the doc comment says 'for tool contact tests' — it was meant to be live, and hand.js's radiiAt (a separate, corrected implementation with a long comment about exactly this failure) is what actually got used.

notReached.title: Leftover scratch variable in the profile-texture hot path
notReached.repro: Nothing visible. It is a note-to-self that was never cleaned up, sitting in the per-frame path.

notReached.title: Hand.pressing is set in three places and read in none
notReached.repro: Nothing visible, but any future code that trusts hand.pressing would be reading a flag no path validates. Note it is also the one field release() clears that grab() would have cleared anyway.

notReached.title: reset()'s dome comment states a coefficient the code does not use
notReached.repro: Not player-visible; a maintenance trap. The number in the comment and the number in the loop underneath it disagree by a factor of two.

notReached.title: The silhouette panel redraws on a frame count, not a clock
notReached.repro: dt is available (it is the argument to _updateThrow) and is used correctly by the two neighbouring throttles — _glazeTick and _statAcc both accumulate dt — but this one adds a hardcoded 0.016 per frame. The comment promises 'a few times a second', which is only true at exactly 60 fps. On the iPad's 120 Hz ProMotion display the panel redraws twice as often as intended, doubling the cost of the one per-frame 2D canvas redraw on the device least able to afford it; on a machine that has already been demoted to 30 fps by the adaptive-quality rung in main.js it redraws half as often, so the outline the player is steering by lags exactly when the frame rate says it should not.

notReached.title: _seenPoint() is a fully documented helper that nothing calls
notReached.repro: `grep -rn _seenPoint src/` returns one hit: this definition. Its docstring describes exactly the job the glaze room needs — 'Where the pointer meets the near face of the pot... the place the player is actually looking at. Null when the pointer is off the clay, in which case the caller falls back to the grazing bearing' — and _updateGlaze instead open-codes the same raycast inline (game.js:2004-2008, building a fresh THREE.Vector3 per frame for the direction and cloning cam.position, which _seenPoint was written to avoid with its cached _sDir/_sOrg scratch vectors). Two smaller dead writes sit alongside it: `this._basis = {}` in the constructor (game.js:193) is never read — _basisAt uses this._heldBasis — and `this.tool.side = 1` (game.js:570) is never read anywhere in src/.

notReached.title: Below ~580px wide the Hide button sits on top of the last tool button and takes its taps
notReached.repro: iPad in Split View (507 CSS px), glaze stage — six tools in the belt. #bare-toggle shares the exact bottom offset of #tools (line 318 has the identical calc) and carries z-index:7 while #tools has none, so it paints and hit-tests over the belt's right end. The bottom-right corner of WIPE FOOT is covered by the Hide button, so a thumb aimed there folds the interface away instead of cleaning the foot.

notReached.title: The kiln panel is 2px NARROWER than the glaze panel, in a rule whose comment says it gets more room
notReached.repro: Desktop window wider than 1153px, kiln stage. The comment directly above reads 'The kiln is a whole phase spent in this panel and nothing else, so it gets the room to be read at a glance' — but the base #context is width:min(392px,34vw) (line 407), so this rule takes 2px away instead of giving room, and below 1153px wide (where both clamp to 34vw) it changes nothing at all. Whatever widening was intended never happened.

notReached.title: Two border-colour rules can never show: the elements they target have border:0
notReached.repro: The floating hand label is supposed to go quiet when no press would land, and the coach pill is supposed to change edge when the step is done. Neither can: line 143's '.slab, .panel, #tools, #coach, #hand{ ... border:0; ... }' zeroes the border width on both, so border-color has nothing to paint. The same applies to line 892, '#coach.done{border-color:var(--celadon);background:#EAF6F0}' — the background does show, the border-colour half is dead.

notReached.title: The interface test harness renders a blank screen, which is why panel bugs keep reaching the iPad
notReached.repro: Open uitest.html. Nothing is drawn. HUD.show() (hud.js:130) only toggles the 'on' class and never removes 'hidden', and .hidden is 'display:none !important' (style.css:169) — so every panel in the harness is display:none, every getBoundingClientRect is zero, and CELADON.layout()-style overlap checks run against an empty screen. The page also has no <meta name="viewport">, so under device emulation it lays out at the legacy 980px default instead of the device width and can never reproduce the 834px or 507px cases where the panels actually collide.

notReached.title: The kiln chimney uses the un-rescaled base brick material, so its bricks are 6.5 cm wide against 24 cm on the kiln directly below it
notReached.repro: Walk the camera round until the kiln is in shot and look up. The chimney is masonry at roughly a quarter the brick size of the kiln body it stands on — the exact 'same wall built out of two different sizes of brick' failure that the comment at studio.js:787-793 says was fixed. Every other kiln slab goes through box(), which clones bm and re-scales the texture from the face size; the chimney is the only mesh that takes bm directly, and bm still carries the repeat set at line 781.

notReached.title: castShadow set on two THREE.Group objects instead of their meshes — the water bucket and the needle tool cast no shadow at all
notReached.repro: Look at the floor next to the bench. The bucket is a 18 cm-wide object standing on a shadow-receiving stone floor lit by the only shadow-casting light in the room (the window key at studio.js:987), and it has no shadow under it — which is the exact 'a pot with no shadow under it does not stand on the wheel, it hovers' problem the wheel's contact-shadow comment at studio.js:325-336 was written about. Same at studio.js:537 for the needle tool group.

notReached.title: Four pot uniforms are declared in JS and in GLSL, never assigned and never read — uRunSmear, uGuide, uK and the fragment/vertex uTime
notReached.repro: No player-facing symptom on its own, but uRunSmear is the hook for the one glaze behaviour the game talks about out loud: game.js:2400 toasts 'You can see it moving through the spy hole. The glaze is running.' and nothing in the surface shader ever smears the glaze downward, because the uniform meant to do it is declared at potMaterial.js:88, declared again in GLSL at line 189, and appears nowhere else in the file. The player is told the glaze ran and then shown a pot on which it did not.

notReached.title: Eight GradeShader uniforms are wired for a fade that does not exist — seven are never written and never read, and uRes is written twice per resize and never read
notReached.repro: No visible symptom — the pass is deliberately identity — but the comment at engine.js:104-107 claims these are 'Kept as identity so the uniforms stay wired for the fade', and there is no fade: a grep across src for uVignette, uGrain, uAberr, uSat, uVigCol, uLift and uGain finds only these declarations and the matching GLSL declaration lines 79-82. uRes is the opposite case, written at engine.js:511 (_buildComposer) and again at 571 (resize, i.e. every frame that changes size) and never read in the fragment body. Only uHaze/uHazeY are live, driven from game.js:1304. Two per-pixel dead computations survive in the same shader: 'float r2 = dot(c,c);' (line 90) and 'float l = dot(col, vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722));' (line 110), neither of which is ever used again.

notReached.title: CameraRig.lock is never assigned true — both orbit() and zoom() guards are dead — and .enabled is written and never read
notReached.repro: `grep -rn 'rig.lock|\.lock *=|rig.enabled' --include=*.js .` over the whole repo minus node_modules and dist returns exactly one hit: engine.js:196 `this.lock = false;`. Nothing ever sets it true, so the guards at engine.js:200 and engine.js:206 can never take their early return. Likewise engine.js:192 `this.enabled = true;` is never read by anything — the only .enabled reads in src are renderer.shadowMap.enabled and eng.smaa.enabled. The visible consequence of the missing lock is that the player can fight every scripted camera move: during the reveal the rig is spinning at autoSpin 0.20 (game.js:2446) and a two-finger drag or a scroll still shoves goalTheta and goalRadius around underneath it.

notReached.title: _pressAt is written every press and read by nothing; its comment describes a feature that was deleted
notReached.repro: `grep -rn '_pressAt' --include=*.js .` (minus node_modules/dist) returns exactly one hit, this write. The comment points at the dab-vs-work timing rule described in the superseded comment block at game.js:302-310 ('once a stroke has been running for a quarter of a second it is work'), which the replacement block at game.js:311-319 removed entirely — onTouchDown now does no timing test at all. So a performance.now() call runs on every single press to feed a field nobody reads, and the comment tells the next reader a rule that is not in the code.

notReached.title: The DIP tooltip still describes the old click-to-dip control and names a mouse the iPad does not have
notReached.repro: Glaze room, tap or hover the DIP tool. The tip says to set the line with the mouse and click. The implementation is the opposite gesture: game.js:2095-2097 arms on press and fires on release, and the comment at game.js:2081-2093 says so explicitly — 'Holding now sets the line and letting go does the dip' — precisely because a finger has no hover and the old click-on-press version gave a tablet player no depth control at all. The tip was never updated, so the one control that was redesigned for touch is still documented as a mouse hover plus a click.
